VOLUME 03 - DATABASE ENGINEERING

Supabase Mental Model
A managed platform built around a real PostgreSQL database

Supabase does not replace PostgreSQL. It gives us PostgreSQL plus managed
platform services around it.

Figure 1 - Supabase platform boundary

Supabase Project

PostgreSQL                 Auth                  Storage

Realtime / APIs

Every Supabase project includes a full PostgreSQL database. Other platform services are layered around it.

Volume 03 - Database Engineering

FULL_STACK_DEVELOPER_2026_COMPLETE - Phase 08                                                               Supabase Mental Model

Book 1 of Phase 08

Start with the correct sentence
CORE MENTAL MODEL

Supabase hosts and manages a PostgreSQL database for TaskFlow. PostgreSQL remains the
database engine.

This distinction matters because the SQL, constraints, indexes, transactions and relational concepts from
Phase 07 remain valid. We are not learning a proprietary database language.

Managed does not mean magical
Supabase manages                                                  You still own
• database infrastructure                                         • schema design
• project dashboard                                               • queries and migrations
• connection endpoints                                            • credentials
• backups/features by plan                                        • application authorization
• pooling infrastructure                                          • performance decisions
• platform integration                                            • safe deployment practices

Three ways developers often touch the database

Figure 2 - Database access paths

Dashboard SQL Editor             →         PostgreSQL

psql / DB tool       →       Connection endpoint             →        PostgreSQL

NestJS later        →        Prisma later         →        PostgreSQL

The same database can be reached through different tools. The tool does not change what the database is.

Dashboard mental map
Area                    Why we care in Phase 08

SQL Editor              Run and save SQL against the project database.

Table Editor            Visual inspection of tables and rows; useful for verification, not a substitute for understanding SQL.

Connect                 Copy the exact direct or pooler connection string.

Database settings       Database password, SSL/certificate and connection-related settings.

Volume 03 - Database Engineering                                                                                Book 1 of Phase 08

FULL_STACK_DEVELOPER_2026_COMPLETE - Phase 08                                                 Supabase Mental Model

Portability lesson
Because the persistence layer is PostgreSQL, much of our schema and SQL knowledge transfers to
another PostgreSQL provider. Supabase-specific services can add value later, but the database
fundamentals are not locked to a unique query language.

DO NOT JUMP AHEAD

The Supabase dashboard may show Auth, Storage, Realtime and Data API features. We will
intentionally ignore most of them now. Seeing a feature is not the same as needing it.

Check your understanding
1. If Supabase disappeared from the architecture diagram, what technology would still define our tables
and SQL? PostgreSQL.
2. Does the Table Editor make constraints unnecessary? No.
3. Will Prisma become the database in Phase 09? No; it will become a typed database-access layer.

FULL_STACK_DEVELOPER_2026_COMPLETE - Phase 08                                                 Create and Inspect the Supabase Project

VOLUME 03 - DATABASE ENGINEERING

Create and Inspect the Supabase
Project
From an empty cloud project to a verified PostgreSQL database

The first professional habit is verification: do not assume the project is ready
because the dashboard loaded.

Figure 1 - Project creation outcome

Supabase account            →       TaskFlow project          →           PostgreSQL database

A project is a platform boundary containing the database and related managed services.

Volume 03 - Database Engineering

FULL_STACK_DEVELOPER_2026_COMPLETE - Phase 08                                                  Create and Inspect the Supabase Project

Book 2 of Phase 08

Before creating anything
Choose a clear project name, use a region appropriate for your development/deployment plan, and
generate a strong database password. Never paste a real password into screenshots, notes, source files or
course submissions.

CREDENTIAL RULE

Your database password is infrastructure access. Treat it more like a server credential than a normal
application setting.

Step-by-step project creation
1. Sign in to Supabase and create or choose an organization.
2. Create a new project named for the learning system, for example taskflow-dev .
3. Select the region intentionally rather than accepting one without noticing.
4. Create/store the database password in a password manager.
5. Wait until project provisioning completes before testing database operations.

Why use a development-oriented name?
Later the course will teach environment separation. Names such as taskflow-dev , taskflow-staging
and taskflow-prod make accidental cross-environment changes easier to notice.

Orient yourself in the dashboard

Figure 2 - Dashboard areas used in Phase 08

SQL Editor                                                    Table Editor
Run queries and schema scripts.                               Inspect rows and table structure visually.

Connect                                                       Database settings
Copy exact host/user/port strings.                            Connection and SSL information.

Use the dashboard as an operational interface; keep the database mental model underneath it.

First verification query
Open SQL Editor and run:

Volume 03 - Database Engineering                                                                                   Book 2 of Phase 08

FULL_STACK_DEVELOPER_2026_COMPLETE - Phase 08                                                 Create and Inspect the Supabase Project

select
current_database() as database_name,
current_user as database_user,
now() as server_time,
version() as postgres_version;

This query does not modify anything. It proves that SQL is executing against the project database and tells
you which PostgreSQL server version your specific project currently runs.

WHY QUERY THE VERSION?

Do not assume the hosted database's major version merely because Phase 07 referenced
PostgreSQL 18 documentation. Hosted platforms can provision different supported major versions.
Ask the server.

Expected result
You should receive one row containing the database name, the connected role, the current server
timestamp and a PostgreSQL version string.

How to verify visually
• SQL Editor returns a result rather than an error.
• Table Editor loads successfully.
• The Connect dialog offers connection methods.
• No secrets have been copied into the repository.

Do not create the final schema yet
Phase 08 uses temporary practice tables. Phase 10 is where TaskFlow's production relational model is
designed deliberately.

FULL_STACK_DEVELOPER_2026_COMPLETE - Phase 08                                                   Connections, Pooling and SSL

VOLUME 03 - DATABASE ENGINEERING

Connections, Pooling and SSL
Choose a connection mode instead of copying whichever URL appears
first

A connection string is infrastructure configuration. Its host, username and port
encode how your client reaches PostgreSQL.

Figure 1 - Connection modes

Persistent backend        →          Direct :5432

IPv4 dev / persistent     →           Session pooler :5432

Serverless / edge     →       Transaction pooler :6543

Supabase documents different connection modes for different runtime behavior.

Volume 03 - Database Engineering

FULL_STACK_DEVELOPER_2026_COMPLETE - Phase 08                                                Connections, Pooling and SSL

Book 3 of Phase 08

Why there are multiple URLs
PostgreSQL has a finite connection budget. Connection poolers sit between clients and the database so
many application clients can share database connections more efficiently.

Three important modes
Mode                  Typical host/port             Use when                                Important property

Direct                db.<ref>.supabase.co:5432     Persistent backend and IPv6-            Direct PostgreSQL
capable environments (or IPv4           session
add-on)

Shared session        pooler host :5432             Persistent client when direct IPv6 is   Session semantics
pooler                                              unavailable; common local-              retained
development choice

Shared                pooler host :6543             Serverless/edge functions with          Transaction pooling;
transaction                                         short-lived connections                 session features are
pooler                                                                                      limited

For this course right now
RECOMMENDED LEARNING CONNECTION

For local Windows development, copy the Session pooler URL from Supabase's Connect dialog
when direct IPv6 connectivity is uncertain. If your environment can reach the direct endpoint reliably,
direct connection is also valid for a persistent backend.

Never manufacture the pooler hostname
Supabase explicitly warns that the shared pooler host can include a cluster index that cannot be inferred
safely from region alone. Copy it from Connect.

Connection-string anatomy
postgresql://USERNAME:PASSWORD@HOST:PORT/DATABASE?sslmode=require

Volume 03 - Database Engineering                                                                      Book 3 of Phase 08

FULL_STACK_DEVELOPER_2026_COMPLETE - Phase 08                                                                       Connections, Pooling and SSL

Part                        Meaning

USERNAME                    Database role. Shared pooler usernames include the project reference.

PASSWORD                    Database password; percent-encode reserved URL characters.

HOST                        Direct database endpoint or pooler endpoint.

PORT                        5432 or 6543 depending on mode.

DATABASE                    Usually postgres for initial course work.

sslmode                     Controls transport encryption behavior.

Password encoding
If a password contains reserved URI characters such as & , # , ? or a space, encode them before
embedding the password inside a URL. Otherwise the parser can mistake password characters for URL
syntax.

SSL
For application connections, set SSL to at least require . Supabase also documents stronger server
verification with verify-full plus the project CA certificate.

SECURITY NUANCE

sslmode=require encrypts the connection, but it does not perform full CA/hostname verification.
verify-full is stronger when configured with the appropriate certificate.

Transaction-pooler limitations
Transaction mode does not preserve session state across transactions and does not support prepared
statements in the same way persistent sessions do. That is why the course will not casually use port 6543
for a long-running NestJS API.

Decision exercise
Scenario                                                                  Likely mode

Local NestJS API on an IPv4-only network                                  Session pooler

Long-running VM with IPv6                                                 Direct

Short-lived serverless functions                                          Transaction pooler, configured for its limitations

lessons.body:
FULL_STACK_DEVELOPER_2026_COMPLETE - Phase 08                                             Secrets and Environment Boundaries

VOLUME 03 - DATABASE ENGINEERING

Secrets and Environment
Boundaries
Keep infrastructure credentials out of source control

A database URL is not "just config" when it contains a password. Its storage location
is part of your security design.

Figure 1 - Secret boundary

Password manager              →       .env on developer machine              →   NestJS / CLI process          →

Supabase Postgres

The secret should reach the process that needs it without becoming source code.

Volume 03 - Database Engineering

FULL_STACK_DEVELOPER_2026_COMPLETE - Phase 08                                   Secrets and Environment Boundaries

Book 4 of Phase 08

The rule
NEVER COMMIT

Do not commit a real DATABASE_URL , database password, service-role key, access token or
downloaded private credential into Git.

Where Phase 08 stores connection information
We will prepare the API directory for a future database URL without using Prisma yet.

# apps/api/.env
DATABASE_URL="postgresql://...real value..."

Then document the variable without the secret:

# apps/api/.env.example
DATABASE_URL=

Git ignore policy
# root or API .gitignore
.env
.env.*
!.env.example

VERIFY, DO NOT ASSUME

From the repository root, run git check-ignore -v apps/api/.env . You want evidence that Git
ignores the file.

PowerShell temporary environment variable
For a one-session test, you can set a process environment variable:

$env:DATABASE_URL = "postgresql://..."

# verify only that a value exists; do not echo it in screenshots
if ($env:DATABASE_URL) { "DATABASE_URL is set" }

This value disappears when that PowerShell process exits. That makes it useful for temporary testing.

Volume 03 - Database Engineering                                                                Book 4 of Phase 08

FULL_STACK_DEVELOPER_2026_COMPLETE - Phase 08                                                           Secrets and Environment Boundaries

Why not put the URL in Next.js?

Figure 2 - Trusted server boundary

Browser                X       Database password

NestJS server              →          Database credentials

Direct database credentials belong in trusted server/tool environments, never the browser bundle.

Our architecture routes browser requests through NestJS. The browser should not receive a privileged
PostgreSQL connection string. Supabase's Data API has a different browser security model built around
public/publishable keys and RLS, but that is not the architecture we are teaching in this phase.

Secret leakage response
1. Assume a committed secret has been exposed even if the repository is private.
2. Rotate/reset the credential.
3. Remove it from current files.
4. Determine whether Git history or CI logs contain it.
5. Do not rely on deleting the latest commit as the only response.

Environment separation preview
development -> taskflow-dev database
staging     -> taskflow-staging database
production -> taskflow-prod database

The same code can run against different infrastructure by changing environment configuration rather than
editing source files.

Checkpoint
[ ] apps/api/.env contains the private URL.
[ ] apps/api/.env.example documents the name only.
[ ] Git ignores the real file.
[ ] No browser-exposed variable contains the database password.

FULL_STACK_DEVELOPER_2026_COMPLETE - Phase 08                                                             Windows psql Workflow

VOLUME 03 - DATABASE ENGINEERING

Connect from Windows with psql
Use the native PostgreSQL client to prove connectivity before adding an
ORM

When a raw PostgreSQL client works, we have isolated the database connection from
framework complexity.

Figure 1 - Connection test isolates the database layer

PowerShell            →             psql                →        Supabase endpoint   →

PostgreSQL

This is a direct database-client test; Next.js, NestJS and Prisma are not involved.

Volume 03 - Database Engineering

FULL_STACK_DEVELOPER_2026_COMPLETE - Phase 08                                               Windows psql Workflow

Book 5 of Phase 08

Why psql matters
psql is PostgreSQL's command-line client. It lets us prove that host, port, role, password and SSL
settings work before introducing Prisma.

Verify the client
In ordinary PowerShell:

psql --version

If Windows cannot find it, Phase 07's PostgreSQL tooling setup or PATH must be corrected before
proceeding.

Recommended connection style
Copy the exact Session pooler values from Supabase. For a secure interactive connection, a parameter-
style command avoids some URI encoding confusion:

psql "sslmode=require host=<POOLER-HOST> port=5432 dbname=postgres user=postgres.<PROJECT-
REF>"

psql will prompt for the password if it is not supplied through another secure mechanism.

WHY PROMPT FOR THE PASSWORD?

It keeps the password out of the command line and reduces the chance that it is captured in shell
history, screenshots or process inspection.

Stronger certificate verification
Supabase documents verify-full using the project's downloaded root certificate:

psql "sslmode=verify-full sslrootcert=C:\path\to\prod-supabase.cer host=<POOLER-HOST>
port=5432 dbname=postgres user=postgres.<PROJECT-REF>"

SQL Editor and the Phase 07
Practice Lab
Move the relational model from paper into a real database

The purpose of this lab is not to build TaskFlow production tables. It is to prove that
relational rules survive outside the textbook.

Figure 1 - Lab loop

Write SQL       →              Run            →         Inspect

→          Change            →            Re-run

Database learning becomes durable when every concept is observed in a real server.

Volume 03 - Database Engineering

FULL_STACK_DEVELOPER_2026_COMPLETE - Phase 08                                       SQL Editor and Practice Lab

Book 6 of Phase 08

Two equivalent learning paths
SQL Editor                                          psql
Convenient in the dashboard, visually shows         Exercises real client/server connectivity and is
result sets, and avoids local connection            closer to automated migration/tooling workflows.
troubleshooting while learning SQL.

Use both. The SQL should remain PostgreSQL SQL in either tool.

Practice schema
create table practice_projects (
id bigint generated always as identity primary key,
name text not null unique,
created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

create table practice_tasks (
id bigint generated always as identity primary key,
project_id bigint not null references practice_projects(id),
title text not null,
completed boolean not null default false,
priority smallint not null default 2 check (priority between 1 and 3),
due_at timestamptz,
created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

What to inspect after creation
• Table names appear in Table Editor and \dt .
• Primary keys exist.
• project_id has a foreign key.
• priority has a check constraint.
• timestamps have defaults.

Volume 03 - Database Engineering                                                            Book 6 of Phase 08

FULL_STACK_DEVELOPER_2026_COMPLETE - Phase 08                                          SQL Editor and Practice Lab

Seed and query
insert into practice_projects (name)
values ('Course'), ('Personal');

insert into practice_tasks (project_id, title, priority)
select id, 'Connect to Supabase', 1
from practice_projects
where name = 'Course';

select p.name as project, t.title, t.priority, t.completed
from practice_projects p
join practice_tasks t on t.project_id = p.id
order by t.priority, t.id;

Observe constraint behavior
Try invalid operations intentionally in the practice tables:

-- should fail: priority outside allowed range
insert into practice_tasks (project_id, title, priority)
values (1, 'Invalid priority', 9);

-- should fail if project 999999 does not exist
insert into practice_tasks (project_id, title)
values (999999, 'Orphan task');

THE LESSON

Application validation improves user experience, but database constraints protect durable state even
when data arrives through another tool or buggy code path.

Transaction exercise
begin;

update practice_tasks
set completed = true
where title = 'Connect to Supabase';

select title, completed from practice_tasks;

rollback;

select title, completed from practice_tasks;

The second query should show the original value because the transaction was rolled back.

VOLUME 03 - DATABASE ENGINEERING

Inspect the Real Database
Learn to verify what actually exists rather than trusting application
assumptions

A professional developer distinguishes "my code says the table exists" from "the
database confirms the table exists."

Figure 1 - Verification layers

Schema expectation             →        Database catalog     →   Actual rows

Verify structure and data at the database layer before blaming higher layers.

Volume 03 - Database Engineering

FULL_STACK_DEVELOPER_2026_COMPLETE - Phase 08                                                     Inspect the Real Database

Book 7 of Phase 08

Inspection is part of development
When persistence bugs appear later, you need to know whether the problem is in the API, ORM, migration,
connection, schema or data. Database inspection narrows the search.

Useful psql inspection commands
\conninfo
\dn
\dt
\d practice_projects
\d practice_tasks
\x auto

Useful SQL inspection queries
select current_database(), current_user, current_schema();

select table_schema, table_name
from information_schema.tables
where table_schema = 'public'
order by table_name;

select constraint_name, constraint_type
from information_schema.table_constraints
where table_name = 'practice_tasks'
order by constraint_type, constraint_name;

Catalog thinking
information_schema exposes standardized metadata views. PostgreSQL also has its own pg_catalog
system catalogs. You do not need to memorize the catalogs now; you need to understand that the
database can describe itself.

Table Editor versus SQL inspection
Tool                Strength                               Risk if overused

Table Editor        Fast visual confirmation               Can hide the SQL/constraint mental model

SQL Editor          Explicit repeatable query logic        Manual dashboard history is not a migration system

psql                Scriptable, close to raw PostgreSQL    CLI requires deliberate connection handling

Query plans preview
Phase 07 introduced indexes. You can ask PostgreSQL how it plans a query:

Volume 03 - Database Engineering                                                                          Book 7 of Phase 08

FULL_STACK_DEVELOPER_2026_COMPLETE - Phase 08                                                 Inspect the Real Database

explain
select *
from practice_tasks
where project_id = 1;

Do not optimize because a plan contains a sequential scan on a tiny practice table. Optimization starts from
real workload and measurements.

Know your server
show server_version;
show timezone;
show search_path;

This prevents assumptions about hosted server configuration from becoming invisible bugs.

Verification checklist
[ ] You can identify which database and role you are using.
[ ] You can list tables without the dashboard.
[ ] You can inspect a table's columns and constraints.
[ ] You can prove whether expected rows exist.
[ ] You can distinguish schema absence from application-fetch failure.

VOLUME 03 - DATABASE ENGINEERING

Connection Troubleshooting and
Database Safety
Debug from the connection outward

Do not rewrite application code when the error is really a host, port, password, SSL
or network problem.

Figure 1 - Connection debugging order

Mode         →              Host/port       →          DNS/IP

→            TLS              →          Credentials    →

SQL

Debug from infrastructure facts toward application behavior.

Volume 03 - Database Engineering

FULL_STACK_DEVELOPER_2026_COMPLETE - Phase 08                                              Troubleshooting and Database Safety

Book 8 of Phase 08

Error-driven troubleshooting
Symptom                            Likely layer                   First checks

Password authentication failed     Credentials                    Correct password? Correct pooled username?
Password URL encoded?

Host cannot be resolved            DNS / copied endpoint          Did you copy the exact host from Connect?

Connection timed out               Network / IP mode /            Direct endpoint may require IPv6; try session pooler
firewall                       for IPv4.

Connection refused                 Host/port/mode                 5432 vs 6543? Wrong endpoint?

SSL/certificate error              TLS configuration              sslmode setting, certificate path, hostname
verification.

Prepared statement/session         Pooling mode                   Are you accidentally on transaction pooler 6543?
behavior breaks

relation does not exist            Schema/search path/            Correct database? schema? Was SQL actually
migration                      applied?

Direct connection and IPv6
Supabase's direct connection is IPv6 by default unless the project has the IPv4 add-on. If your local ISP or
runtime is IPv4-only, a direct host can fail even when the credentials are correct. The shared session pooler
is the usual IPv4-friendly alternative.

Do not confuse CORS with database connectivity
CORS is a browser HTTP security mechanism. psql connects using the PostgreSQL protocol. If psql
cannot reach Supabase, changing NestJS CORS settings cannot fix it.

Do not use a browser-exposed database password
If a connection works only after putting the database URL into NEXT_PUBLIC_... , the solution is worse
than the problem. That would expose a privileged credential to browser JavaScript.

Safety when using SQL Editor
• Read destructive statements before running them.
• Use transactions for risky multi-step changes when appropriate.
• Do not casually run production SQL copied from an AI or forum.
• Prefer repeatable migration files once Prisma enters the course.
• Keep development and production projects visually distinct.

Volume 03 - Database Engineering                                                                           Book 8 of Phase 08

FULL_STACK_DEVELOPER_2026_COMPLETE - Phase 08                                                 Troubleshooting and Database Safety

RLS and the public schema - preview only
Supabase can expose tables through its Data APIs. Browser/client-library access has a different security
model involving grants and Row Level Security. Our TaskFlow architecture uses NestJS as the business/
API boundary, so we will not design RLS policies in this phase. We will revisit database exposure and
authorization in the security/authentication volumes.

IMPORTANT

Do not interpret "we are not using RLS yet" as "RLS does not matter." It means the course is
separating concerns so authentication and authorization are taught with enough context.

Smallest-correction rule
If the username is wrong, fix the username. If the host is wrong, copy the correct host. Do not reinstall
Node, recreate NestJS or reset the database when the evidence points to a connection parameter.

Volume 03 - Database Engineering

Book 9 of Phase 08

Level 1 - Follow
1. Create or open the TaskFlow development Supabase project.
2. Run the server-information query in SQL Editor.
3. Copy the Session pooler settings without exposing the password.
4. Connect with psql .
5. Create the temporary practice tables.

7. Drop the temporary tables.

Level 2 - Modify
1. Add an optional notes text column to practice_tasks .
2. Add a new project and two tasks.
3. Write a query that lists unfinished tasks ordered by priority.
4. Use a transaction to change two rows, inspect them, then roll back.

Level 3 - Implement
Without copying the lesson SQL, create a temporary table called practice_tags and a join table
representing a many-to-many relationship between practice tasks and tags. Add sensible keys and
constraints, seed data, then write a join that returns task title + tag name.

Level 4 - Engineer
Design a short connection strategy note for three future deployments:

• local NestJS development on IPv4-only home internet
• a persistent container/VM with IPv6 connectivity
• a serverless worker that opens many short-lived connections

For each, choose direct/session/transaction mode and explain the tradeoff. Do not choose by memorized
port number alone.

Debugging scenarios
Scenario A - Authentication failure
psql reports password authentication failure. List the evidence you would check before resetting the
entire project.

Scenario B - Direct host timeout
The credentials are correct but the direct endpoint times out from home internet. What network capability
might be missing, and which connection mode would you test next?

List database/schema/connection assumptions that should be verified before editing the ORM model.

Architecture oral exam
1. Is Supabase the ORM? Explain.
2. Why can direct and session-pooler URLs both use port 5432 but have different hosts/usernames?
3. Why is port 6543 not automatically "better"?
4. Why should the browser never receive our PostgreSQL password?
5. What does sslmode=require protect, and what does it not fully verify?
6. What does psql prove before Prisma is installed?
7. Why do we query the actual server version instead of assuming it?

[ ] Supabase development project exists.
[ ] You can explain Supabase vs PostgreSQL.
[ ] You can choose a connection mode deliberately.
[ ] Database credentials are outside Git.
[ ] psql connects over SSL.
[ ] You ran Phase 07 relational SQL against the real database.
[ ] You inspected tables and constraints.
[ ] You intentionally cleaned up practice objects.
[ ] You can diagnose common connection failures by layer.
[ ] You can explain what Prisma will add next.

Debugging Workshop — Phase 08: Supabase PostgreSQL

Goal
Learn to diagnose this phase's failures systematically instead of reinstalling packages, changing random configuration, or copying a fix without understanding it.

The debugging loop
1. Reproduce the failure with the smallest reliable action.
2. Capture the exact symptom: command, status code, stack trace, network request, database state, or UI state.
3. Locate the earliest boundary where actual behavior diverges from expected behavior.
4. Form one hypothesis.
5. Change one variable.
6. Re-run the same reproduction.
7. Keep the fix only if the evidence supports the hypothesis.

Boundary walk
Application -> connection string/pooler -> Supabase Postgres -> database objects -> dashboard/observability

Start at the visible symptom and walk backward. Do not debug the database when the browser never sent the request. Do not debug React state when the API is returning a deterministic 403. The boundary walk tells you which evidence to collect next.

Failure drill 1 — Committing database credentials
Create or imagine this failure in a safe development environment. Write the expected symptom first. Then list the two or three observations that would distinguish this failure from neighboring causes. Repair it with the smallest change and verify the original reproduction no longer fails.

Failure drill 2 — Using the wrong connection mode for serverless/concurrent workloads
Create or imagine this failure in a safe development environment. Write the expected symptom first. Then list the two or three observations that would distinguish this failure from neighboring causes. Repair it with the smallest change and verify the original reproduction no longer fails.

Failure drill 3 — Treating dashboard clicks as schema migration history
Create or imagine this failure in a safe development environment. Write the expected symptom first. Then list the two or three observations that would distinguish this failure from neighboring causes. Repair it with the smallest change and verify the original reproduction no longer fails.

Failure drill 4 — Pointing preview environments at production data
Create or imagine this failure in a safe development environment. Write the expected symptom first. Then list the two or three observations that would distinguish this failure from neighboring causes. Repair it with the smallest change and verify the original reproduction no longer fails.

Do not hide the evidence
Avoid immediately clearing caches, deleting lockfiles, resetting the database, disabling security checks, or reinstalling everything. Those actions may erase the evidence that teaches you what was wrong. Use them only after you can explain why they are relevant.

Mission
Rebuild the capability of Phase 08 without following the exact code line-by-line. The goal is transfer: can you use the ideas when the variable names, UI, or route shape changes?

Required outcome
Operate Supabase as managed PostgreSQL with deliberate project, connection, pooling, dashboard, and environment boundaries.

Required artifact

Constraints
• Start from the previous phase checkpoint or a fresh branch.
• Use the course architecture boundaries, but do not copy the reference implementation until after your first attempt.
• Keep changes scoped to the capability.
• Preserve validation, authorization, error handling, and observability expectations already earned in earlier phases.
• Record any design decision where more than one implementation is reasonable.

Acceptance criteria
• Can explain direct vs pooled connections.
• Can identify public vs secret Supabase values.
• Can diagnose connectivity.

5. Test connectivity from the API environment and diagnose a deliberately incorrect host/port/password.
6. Document how local, staging, and production projects will remain separate.

Self-review
Compare your implementation to the reference only after the acceptance criteria pass. Differences are not automatically mistakes. For each difference, ask: does it preserve the same contract, security boundary, correctness, maintainability, and operational behavior? Keep the alternative when you can justify it with evidence.

Stretch challenge
Change one assumption: more users, a second tenant, a slow network, an expired session, a concurrent mutation, a deployment restart, or a failed dependency. Predict whether your design still behaves correctly. If not, document the next architectural improvement rather than adding complexity blindly.

Phase exit
Run the relevant checks, inspect Git diff, and write a three-sentence summary: what the system can do now, which boundary owns the new responsibility, and which failure you now know how to diagnose. Only then mark the phase complete.
